run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-17T01:04:03Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend is explained by a restart of Deployment ad at 2026-11-17T01:03:00Z (pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt). The new ad pod was created at 01:03:00-01:03:02 and the old serving pod was killed at 01:03:02, but the new ad process only logged "Ad service starting." at 01:07:42.97 and "Ad service started, listening on 8080" at 01:09:22.98, with its first request log at 01:10:44.6; Deployment ad defines no readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe and no minReadySeconds, so the rollout retired the only serving replica while its replacement was not yet listening. In exactly those minutes ad's own oteldemo.AdService/GetAds server-span increases are 0 while frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds client spans carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR, together with frontend's GET /api/data, executing api route (pages) /api/data, POST /api/checkout, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and tcp.connect error spans, and frontend-proxy's own ingress and router frontend egress error spans; the burst ends around 01:12-01:14 when ad serves again. A second, shorter gap follows the simultaneous restart of Deployment payment at 01:02:59 (checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge client error spans, payment's own Charge server-span increase 0 in the same minute), whose logs show it only began completing charges at 01:07:33. Two fault-injection settings in ConfigMap flagd-config (adFailure=on, paymentUnreachable=on) were considered but remain hypotheses: ad served normally again and frontend GetAds succeeded while the ConfigMap still read those values when it was read later in the Run, so they do not match the observed connection-level gap. fraud-detection was OOMKilled at 01:04:46 (restart 1) on the same node, but no fraud-detection error spans or checkout-to-fraud errors were observed, so it is recorded as a separate failure, not this cause. Why the new ad container took about 4.7 minutes to reach its first log line is not established: this target exposes no node CPU/memory series and no container CPU-throttling series.

claims.text: frontend error spans (STATUS_CODE_ERROR) were 0 in every returned bucket up to and including the 01:03 bucket and became non-zero from the 01:04 bucket onward, narrowing to 0 again by the 01:14-01:17 buckets; the error span_names for that service include grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, GET /api/data, executing api route (pages) /api/data, GET, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, POST /api/checkout, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout, POST and tcp.connect.

frontend-proxy's own error spans on operations "ingress" and "router frontend egress" were 0 before 01:04, rose from the 01:04 bucket (19.2 and 16.8 in the 3-minute increase) to peaks of 256.8 and 256.8 in the 01:08 bucket, and were back near 0 at 01:15-01:16.

Deployment ad in namespace otel-demo carries pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T01:03:00Z with image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad and replicas 1; Deployment payment carries restartedAt=2026-11-17T01:02:59Z with image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment.

otel-demo events show the ad rollout: Deployment ad ScalingReplicaSet "Scaled up replica set ad-5f8dd7c58d from 0 to 1" at 01:03:00, pod ad-5f8dd7c58d-rtbj5 Scheduled 01:03:00, container Created and Started 01:03:02, and ScalingReplicaSet "Scaled down replica set ad-554b849958 from 1 to 0" at 01:03:02 with Pod ad-554b849958-6z62j Killing "Stopping container ad" also at 01:03:02; the payment rollout shows the same pattern (pod payment-5d565cf9b-8gwcn started 01:03:03, pod payment-55766d76b9-9fxhp Stopping at 01:03:03).

The new ad container in pod ad-5f8dd7c58d-rtbj5 wrote its first log line "Ad service starting." at 2026-11-17T01:07:42.972878021Z and "Ad service started, listening on 8080" at 2026-11-17T01:09:22.975023314Z, with its first request log at 01:10:44.600311095Z; all 218 lines it produced inside the window are after 01:07:42, although the container was Started at 01:03:02.

ad's own server operation oteldemo.AdService/GetAds had STATUS_CODE_UNSET increases of roughly 90-116 per bucket through the 01:04 bucket, then exactly 0 in the 01:06 through 01:12 buckets, and 100 again in the 01:14 bucket; in those same buckets frontend's client operation grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds carried STATUS_CODE_ERROR (8 at 01:04, then 126, 78, 120, 112, 96, 126, 48) with its STATUS_CODE_UNSET counterpart at 0, returning to UNSET (40, then 98) at 01:13-01:14.

Deployment ad's pod template defines no readinessProbe, no livenessProbe and no startupProbe, minReadySeconds is unset, strategy is RollingUpdate with maxSurge 25% and maxUnavailable 25%, and the ad container's resources are limits cpu 50m / memory 450Mi with requests cpu 10m / memory 225Mi.

checkout's own spans show oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge in STATUS_CODE_ERROR in the 01:06 bucket (64 each) while payment's grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge server-span increase was 0 in that bucket and 69.4 in the 01:07 bucket, and payment's logs show "Charge request received." paired with "Transaction complete." from 01:07:33 onward.

ConfigMap flagd-config in otel-demo holds demo.flagd.json in which adFailure has defaultVariant "on" (description "Fail ad service") and paymentUnreachable has defaultVariant "on" (description "Payment service is unavailable"), while every other flag in that file is "off"; both Deployments ad and payment inject FLAGD_HOST=flagd and FLAGD_PORT=8013.

Pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-n79gv on node i-068d8c8f254eed0b1 has restartCount 1 with lastState terminated reason "OOMKilled", exitCode 137, finishedAt 2026-11-17T01:04:46Z, matching events "Created container: fraud-detection" and "Started container fraud-detection" at 01:04:47, and its container memory working set fell from 413560832 at 01:05 to 212713472 at 01:06.

A per-service error-span query across ad, checkout, product-catalog, recommendation, cart, payment, shipping, currency, quote, email and fraud-detection returned error series only for ad (flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream about 1 per window and one ResolveBoolean point), checkout (PlaceOrder and PaymentService/Charge), fraud-detection (flagd EventStream about 1 per window) and payment (0 on GET, dns.lookup and tcp.connect); no error series was returned for product-catalog, cart, currency, quote, email or shipping.

At the time of the query all five nodes were Ready with DiskPressure, PIDPressure and MemoryPressure status False (reason KubeletHasSufficientMemory on i-068d8c8f254eed0b1), and the target lists only container_memory_* series for memory, with no node-level memory or CPU metric names.

The current otel-demo pod listing shows frontend-675fd7b5c5-68tcg, ad-5f8dd7c58d-rtbj5 and payment-5d565cf9b-8gwcn all Running and ready with restartCount 0 on node i-068d8c8f254eed0b1, and shipping-75d58f5d84-mh42p, checkout-5dccddf8bb-vxwlj and currency-5d455cf6f7-zmkrv also ready with 0 restarts.

The roughly 4.7-minute gap between container start (01:03:02) and the first "Ad service starting." log line (01:07:42.97) is plausibly explained by CPU starvation of the ad process under its cpu 50m limit, since the same node also runs kafka, postgresql and the otel-collector; this is unconfirmed because no container CPU-throttling or node CPU series exists in this target.

The flagd-config fault-injection settings adFailure=on ("Fail ad service") and paymentUnreachable=on ("Payment service is unavailable") remain candidates, but they do not match the observed failure path: frontend's ad calls failed while ad emitted no server spans at all because its process had not yet started listening, and both ad traffic and checkout-to-payment Charge calls had recovered while the ConfigMap still read those values when it was read later in this Run.

Node-level resource pressure on i-068d8c8f254eed0b1 around 01:03-01:05, where both replacement pods were scheduled and where fraud-detection was OOMKilled at 01:04:46, could have slowed both new containers' startup, but this cannot be verified because the target has no node memory or CPU series and node conditions read later show no MemoryPressure.

fraud-detection's OOMKill at 01:04:46 is not the cause of the frontend error-rate alert: no fraud-detection error spans appear in the window beyond a constant background flagd EventStream error, and checkout's failing calls in that period are its PaymentService/Charge client spans rather than a fraud call.

Give the ad and payment containers a readinessProbe and startupProbe plus a non-zero minReadySeconds so a rollout cannot stop the old pod before the new process is listening, and raise ad's cpu limit (currently 50m; payment 20m) or measure its cold-start CPU requirement.

Have a human confirm whether the flagd-config settings adFailure=on and paymentUnreachable=on are intentional, and review the fraud-detection container's memory limit against its observed working set near 413 MB before its OOMKill, since both are unattended risks even though neither explains this alert.

gaps: Why the new ad container took about 4.7 minutes (container Started 01:03:02, first log line 01:07:42.97) is not established: the target exposes only container_memory_* series and no node CPU/memory or container CPU-throttling metric, and no event or container restart explains it.
The alerting rule named RequestErrorRate returned nothing from list_prometheus_rules (status no_data), so the exact alert expression and the series it aggregates could not be verified.

A histogram_quantile query on rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket for payment, ad and checkout returned no_data, so gRPC server latency and status-code label detail could not be compared against a baseline and no latency claim is made.

Jaeger returned no traces for frontend, ad or checkout in the incident window (traces_search and traces_search_by_tags returned no_data), so span-level error text and parent-child call edges could not be verified; operation co-occurrence is reported without asserting a parent-child relationship.
Application logs from the frontend container could not be read: the fetch for frontend-675fd7b5c5-68tcg returned no_data with 0 lines read, so the exact error text frontend logged is unknown.

The change_history integration is not available, so when and by whom the flagd-config flags (adFailure, paymentUnreachable) and the kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt annotations on Deployments ad and payment were set cannot be verified.
Secrets are unreadable, so any configuration held only in a Secret could not be checked.

Whether product-catalog, cart, currency, quote, email and shipping were entirely free of errors is unknown: the error-span query returned no series for them, and a series that is not returned is unknown rather than zero.

Prometheus data for these series ended between 01:14 and 01:22 depending on the query (freshness 210-737 s) and some minute buckets (for example 01:05 and 01:13) were absent, so behaviour after those cut-offs is unknown; the ad and payment log reads also stopped at 01:12:47 and 01:12:40.

The agent-level error-span query for names matching fraud returned no_data, so absence of fraud-detection error spans is established only through the broader per-service error query, not a name-matched fraud query.
next_steps: Compare ad and payment container CPU throttling and CPU usage series (cAdvisor container_cpu_* is not currently available in this target) to test the CPU-starvation explanation for the slow start.

Confirm with the operator or CI who issued the 01:03:00Z and 01:02:59Z rollout restarts of Deployments ad and payment, and whether that was intended to accompany the flagd-config values adFailure=on and paymentUnreachable=on.
Review AdService startup behaviour with OTLP export enabled (about 100 s between "Ad service starting." and "listening on 8080") to see whether collector connectivity delays readiness.
Check whether the fraud-detection memory limit sits below its observed working set near 413 MB, and treat its OOMKill as a separate item from this alert.
